questions.q: The main determinants of SRAS are:
options: The price level and production costs
questions.why: The price level moves along the curve, and costs shift it.

questions.q: Match each event to its effect on SRAS.
pairs: Wages rise with no rise in productivity
questions.why: Costs up: left. Costs down: right.

questions.q: Why does higher productivity shift SRAS to the right?
options: The cost of each unit falls
questions.why: More output from the same pay lowers unit costs.

questions.q: A change in the price level causes a movement along the SRAS curve.
How could a fall in the pound shift the UK's SRAS?
options: Left, as imported raw materials cost more
It has no effect on SRAS
questions.why: UK firms pay more for what they import.

questions.q: Explain how a general rise in money wages could affect the price level.

ideas.label: Wages are a cost, so firms' costs rise and SRAS shifts left

questions.model: Wages are a cost for firms, so costs rise and SRAS shifts left. Firms pass this on, so the price level rises.
questions.why: Pay is a cost as well as an income.

tests.answer: Firms' costs rise, so SRAS shifts left and the price level rises.
